card.title: WINDHUND DIVISION
card.text: Can operate again after it attacks and destroys a unit.
card.flavorText: The 116th Panzer Division was known as the Windhund Division, or Greyhound Division. It was formed in western Germany in 1944 from the remnants of the 16th Panzergrenadier Division and the 179th Reserve Panzer Division. Its motto praised speed and toughness, fitting a formation created during a year when Germany needed mobile reserves against the growing Allied threat in the west. The division entered combat after the Normandy landings and fought during the Battle of Normandy. After the Allied breakout, it was caught in the Falaise Pocket. Along with the 2nd SS Panzer Division, it helped keep an escape route open for other German units, but it escaped with only about 600 infantry men and 12 tanks still intact. After refitting, the Windhund Division fought at Aachen and in the Hürtgen Forest, where it helped retake the town of Schmidt from the US 28th Infantry Division. It later joined the Ardennes offensive, but damaged bridges, resistance, and fuel problems slowed its advance. In 1945, it fought west of the Rhine, then was trapped in the Ruhr Pocket. Most of the division surrendered to the US Ninth Army in April.
